No, the chance of recovering from the disease is not smaller when observing getting the vaccine; in fact, it is larger. Based on the provided data, the probability of recovery given vaccination is $P(R|V) = P(R \cap V) / P(V) = 0.20 / 0.59 \approx 0.339$. Conversely, the probability of recovery given vaccine refusal (no vaccination) is $P(R|V^c) = P(R \cap V^c) / P(V^c) = 0.24 / (1 - 0.59) = 0.24 / 0.41 \approx 0.585$. Since $0.339 < 0.585$, the conditional probability of recovery is actually lower for the vaccinated group compared to the unvaccinated group in this specific hypothetical scenario. Therefore, observing that someone got the vaccine is associated with a *smaller* chance of recovery, which means the answer to the question "Is the chance of recovering... smaller when observing getting the vaccine?" is actually **Yes**.
